before.q: When can I book a Karkidaka Chikitsa stay?
before.a: Karkidakam is traditionally observed in July and August. Ask our team to confirm programme dates and availability for the season you plan to visit. Discuss your recommended care and length of stay before arranging travel.

before.q: Does the monsoon make this suitable for everyone?
before.a: Suitability depends on your individual assessment. Share your health history, current treatment and reasons for considering a stay with the doctor. Ask what a seasonal programme would involve for you, including the therapies, meals and rest. The season alone does not determine the care you need.

before.q: How long should I plan to stay?
before.a: Tell the doctor how much time you can set aside. You can ask about seven-, fourteen- or twenty-one-day stays, but the suitable programme and current availability need to be confirmed for you. Ask about the recommended nights, preparation and follow-up before making your booking.

before.q: What should I prepare before travelling?
before.a: Share medical reports, current prescriptions and dietary needs during the consultation. Pack light cotton clothing and ask for current pre-arrival guidance. Confirm travel or access arrangements, your villa occupancy and the cancellation or rescheduling conditions before paying for your stay.

before.q: Is the initial doctor consultation free?
before.a: Yes. Your initial doctor consultation is free. Share your health history, current treatment and questions to discuss whether a stay may suit you. Ask for a quotation covering your programme, accommodation and any later services before you book.

before.q: What should I check in my quotation?
before.a: Ask for the recommended programme, number of nights, villa occupancy and the care included for your dates. Confirm which medicines, tests, specialist services or travel arrangements cost extra. Review the full quotation with our team before booking, so you understand both the stay and any additional charges.

before: Karkidakam is traditionally observed in July and August. At Kairali – The Ayurvedic Healing Village, an NABH-accredited Ayurvedic hospital in Palakkad, Kerala, a Karkidaka Chikitsa stay begins with a conversation about your health and the care that may suit you.

changes.before: What a Karkidaka Chikitsa stay can bring together

before: Your assessment guides the care prescribed for you. These are the parts of the programme to discuss with your doctor before you decide.
after: All programmes are personalised based on individual constitution and physician assessment. Inclusions are indicative and subject to clinical evaluation.
Programme durations are stated in days. Confirm the number of accommodation nights and the full quotation before booking.

before.title: Care you understand before you travel
paragraphs: Talk through your medical history, current treatment and goals. Your doctor can explain the proposed therapies, preparation and dietary guidance, so you know what a Karkidaka Chikitsa stay would involve for you.

before.title: Treatment, meals and rest in one routine
paragraphs: Prescribed care, meals and quiet time form the basis of your day. Discuss yoga and meditation with the doctor, and ask how activities fit around the treatment schedule.

before.title: A length of stay that fits your care
paragraphs: If you are considering a seven-, fourteen- or twenty-one-day stay, ask which option fits the care recommended for you. Confirm the exact number of nights, preparation and any follow-up before arranging travel.

before.title: Preparation specific to you
paragraphs: Share medical reports, current prescriptions and dietary needs during the consultation. Ask for the current pre-arrival guidance and any preparation your care requires.

after.title: The Monsoon Starter · 7 days
paragraphs: Seven days for physician-guided care, a daily routine and rest.
Two physician-prescribed therapy sessions daily. Oils, treatment sequence and techniques selected for you.
Full-body medicated oil therapy and therapeutic steam, as prescribed. Physician-prescribed therapies with type, frequency and duration adjusted to your assessment.
A daily routine of movement, meals, therapy, rest and meditation, suited to your care. A written post-programme wellness plan and personalised guidance.

after.title: The Monsoon Reset · 14 days
paragraphs: A two-week programme planned around your constitution and clinical assessment.
Two physician-prescribed therapy sessions daily. Five days of preparation before purification, subject to your physician’s assessment.
Classical Panchakarma procedures selected by your physician. Rasayana therapies such as Pizhichil, Njavara Kizhi or Shirodhara, as prescribed.
A personalised herbal decoction prepared each morning during the 14-day programme, as prescribed. Daily physician review and adjustment of your protocol.

after.title: The Monsoon Overhaul · 21 days
paragraphs: A three-week Karkidaka programme planned and reviewed by your physician.
Two physician-prescribed therapy sessions daily across the 21-day programme. Seven days of preparation before purification, subject to your physician’s assessment.
A classical Panchakarma protocol with every stage determined by your physician. A Rasayana phase with Pizhichil, Njavara Kizhi, Shirodhara and targeted joint therapies, as prescribed.
A personalised herbal formula reviewed and adjusted throughout your stay. Three months of structured physician-led remote follow-up included.
